newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans new laws to boost production.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans new laws to boost production.

text.p: Ukraine plans a new legal framework to support domestic producers as part of a three-year economic plan to revive the skrinking sector, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Tuesday.

Lazarenko, presenting the plan to parliament, also said the government had prepared 40 large projects to boost production, including creating financial groups to support companies such as Ukrainian engine-makers and bus manufacturers and to restructure existing production.
Value added tax on imported goods would be retained.

"In our aim to increase production we will have to balance the economy with government regulation, reduce dependence on foreign goods, raise living standards and meet the needs of the population," Lazarenko said.

He said the fall in production had reached crisis levels and required tough measures. The former Soviet republic's economy has shrunk progressively since independence in 1991 and only slight growth is predicted next year.
Industrial output was nine percent lower in September than a year earlier.
"Backing our producers and maintaining national production is the chief position of our government," Lazarenko said.

Lazarenko said Ukraine had in recent months stepped up aircraft production, was moving ahead with upgrading its telephone system through foreign investment, and was seeking strategic foreign investment for various enterprises.
Tax reform, promised for 1997, would alleviate taxation pressure on producers, Lazarenko added.
Economy Minister Vasyl Hureyev revealed details of the plan late least month.
